questions.prompt: What formal mathematical setting is quantum mechanics defined in?
questions.explanation: A Hilbert space is the complete, formal complex vector space setting quantum mechanics is defined in.

questions.prompt: What two defining properties must a valid density operator have?
options: Positive semi-definite and trace equal to 1
questions.explanation: A density operator must be positive semi-definite with trace equal to 1 to be a valid quantum state description.

questions.prompt: Why must a quantum channel be 'completely positive,' not just 'positive'?
options: To correctly describe how the channel acts on part of a larger entangled system
Complete positivity only matters for classical channels
It ensures the channel runs faster
questions.explanation: Complete positivity ensures the channel produces valid states even when acting on part of a larger entangled system, a stronger requirement than simple positivity.

questions.prompt: What does Von Neumann entropy quantify?
options: The uncertainty or 'mixedness' of a density operator
The speed of a quantum gate
The number of physical qubits available
questions.explanation: Von Neumann entropy extends Shannon entropy to quantum states, quantifying uncertainty/mixedness — also used to measure entanglement.

questions.prompt: What does a POVM generalize beyond simple projective measurement?
options: The most general possible description of a quantum measurement, including imperfect real devices
questions.explanation: A POVM generalizes projective measurement to accurately model the most general, including imperfect, quantum measurement devices.
